text:
B: Alright. Darren.
A: Hello. Gillian. Is this the last one?
B: Think so. Thank God. How long's it been, an hour?
A: About that. Erm, I still don't really know what it's for.
B: No, me neither. Not sure what they're after, to be honest. Where are you, then?
A: Bramhall. Stockport. It's a nice area. You're Basingstoke, I think. Everyone seems to be Basingstoke.
B: Yeah, half of them are. Brighton Hill. I run a builders' merchant.
A: Oh, right. I'm an optometrist. Three days a week.
B: Eyes. Right. I should probably get mine done. Never have.
A: Never? How old are you?
B: Thirty-six.
A: Then go. It's not just glasses, it's eye health, blood pressure shows up in the back of your eye, diabetes, all sorts. Men your age never come in until something's wrong, and then it's, oh, I've had this headache for three weeks. You'd be surprised what we pick up. Erm, yeah. Sorry. Go and get it done.
B: Alright, alright. I'll book it. With the MOT.
A: Ha. Do both.
B: Blood pressure, though. My dad had a heart attack at fifty-eight. So that's, er... that's why I go the gym, mostly.
A: Oh. Martin's dad had one too. My husband. And Martin likes a drink, so I do worry, if I'm honest.
B: Does he do anything? Exercise?
A: He watches City. Does that count?
B: Not really, no.
A: No. That's what I tell him.
B: Yeah. Erm, yeah, so... you away this year?
A: Algarve. Same place we always go. I hate flying, though. I'm a nightmare at the airport, I check the passports every five minutes.
B: Same. I check them about four times before we leave the house. Kelly goes mad.
A: Martin says I'll wear the pages out.
B: Ha. We do Tenerife. All-inclusive. Sunbed, pool, done. I don't want to be traipsing round looking at churches.
A: No. We did Rome once, it was a lovely hotel, five-star, but the walking. My feet.
B: That's why I don't do city breaks. Don't see the point.
A: Erm, have you got kids? Sorry, I've asked everyone that.
B: A lad, Alfie, nine. He's with his mum. I have him every other weekend.
A: Oh. That's hard.
B: Yeah. It is. Erm. He's good, though. Into his football.
A: Mine have both gone now, so I'm sort of rattling round the house. Leeds and Nottingham.
B: Quiet, then.
A: Very. Just me and the dog on my days off. Erm, yeah. That's it really.
B: Yeah, so... what you having for dinner?
A: Tea? Spag bol, probably. Half six.
B: Tea, yeah. You lot. We're spag bol midweek too.
A: Well, there you go. Something in common. Apart from the passports.
